Maya S.: heads up — customer acme-inc reported a sudden spike in 429s starting ~2026-02-18 09:03 UTC after they switched to the 'fast-chat-3' route. They say it looks like rate limiting / quota exhaustion even though they had reserved capacity. Full error snippet from their app:

Maya S.: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "Request throttled",
  "reason": "per_customer_route_quota_exhausted",
  "route": "/v1/generate/fast-chat-3",
  "customer_id": "acme-inc-42"
}
```

Maya S.: they included a sample curl that reproduces it from their side (hitting our hosted region us-west-2).

Maya S.: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/fast-chat-3 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}'
```

Maya S.: asking: 1) why did their reserved capacity not prevent throttling? 2) how to show them metrics/dashboards that attribute throttling to a route/model/customer, and 3) any short-term mitigations?

David R. (eng): cc @Priya K. (SRE) @Sasha L. (infra) — initial thought: could be per-route burst guard or global per-customer hard quota kicking in. Need to check quota enforcement logs and the traffic shaping rules for fast-chat-3.

Priya K. (SRE): on it. Maya, can you paste the customer's customer_id and the approximate window of the spikes? Also did they see 429s from a single API key or many?

Maya S.: customer_id acme-inc-42, spike started 2026-02-18T09:03:12Z, lasted ~12m. They said it looked like a single API key (one service account) but multiple concurrent connections (~40).

Sasha L. (infra): quick defs — we have three rate layers: 1) per-API-key token bucket (burst config), 2) per-customer daily/monthly quota, and 3) per-route soft-shed when model capacity is overloaded. Reserved Dedicated capacity reduces the soft-shed threshold but doesn't disable per-key buckets. If they used a single key with many concurrent requests, token-bucket bursts could be exhausted.

David R. (eng): can you pull the quota-enforcer logs for customer acme-inc-42 around that timestamp? Look for events: QUOTA_EXHAUST, TOKEN_BUCKET_EMPTY, or ROUTE_SHED. The log lines include fields: ts, customer_id, route, model_variant, reason, current_tokens, allowed_rate.

Priya K. (SRE): pulled logs from quotas-service: ```
2026-02-18T09:03:13Z quota-enforcer INFO {customer:acme-inc-42 route:/v1/generate/fast-chat-3 reason:TOKEN_BUCKET_EMPTY key:sa-acme-main current_tokens:0 allowed_rate:20rps}  
2026-02-18T09:03:14Z quota-enforcer INFO {customer:acme-inc-42 route:/v1/generate/fast-chat-3 reason:QUOTA_EXHAUST key:sa-acme-main remaining_daily:0}  
2026-02-18T09:05:01Z router WARN {route:fast-chat-3 model:fast-chat-3-quant reason:SOFT_SHED active_conns:230 capacity:200} 
```

Priya K. (SRE): looks like token bucket drained first, then daily quota hit (they were near daily commit), and router soft-shed started a minute later when overall cluster utilization climbed. So multiple layers triggered.

Maya S.: helpful — customer insists this is wrong because they have Dedicated reserved capacity for fast-chat-3. How do I explain the interaction?

Sasha L. (infra): concise explanation: Dedicated guarantees capacity at the serving layer (GPU pools) but we still enforce per-key and per-customer logical quotas upstream to protect fairness. Their dedicated pool prevents being evicted from GPUs, but it doesn't auto-increase their token-bucket burst or lift their daily quota. If they want higher sustained and burst RPS they need a quota bump (and possibly a higher burst config).

David R. (eng): add that reserved capacity variants are supposed to route first, but if traffic pattern is > configured burst and their daily limit is exceeded, the gateway will still 429. We should show them evidence (logs + metrics) and offer tuning options: increase token-bucket size, raise allowed_rate, and/or increase daily quota.

Maya S.: ok. Customer asked for a dashboard showing attribution: "which 429s are due to token-bucket vs quota vs route-shed, and which model/route caused it". Any existing panels we can point to?

Priya K. (SRE): yes. On Grafana -> "Limits & Throttling" board we have panels: "429 by reason (rate/quota/shed)", "Token bucket remaining by customer", "Route soft-shed events", and "Per-customer RPS vs committed RPS". Query examples below.

Priya K. (SRE): PromQL snippet for 429 breakdown:
```promql
sum by(reason) (increase(api_responses_total{code="429"}[5m]))
```

Priya K. (SRE): Token bucket remaining (per-customer):
```promql
min_over_time(token_bucket_tokens{customer_id="acme-inc-42"}[15m])
```

Priya K. (SRE): Route soft-shed events (counter):
```promql
increase(route_shed_events_total{route="/v1/generate/fast-chat-3"}[10m])
```

Sasha L. (infra): to attribute to model variant, include label model_variant in the 429 and shed metrics. Eg: api_responses_total{code="429", model_variant=~"fast-chat-3.*"}. Also make a panel that groups 429s by customer_id and reason.

David R. (eng): for customer-facing view, we typically produce a single chart: stacked 429s over time with color for reason and hover that shows model and route. Also attach a CSV export of raw events for the window.

Maya S.: can we produce a small packet for acme (dashboard excerpt + log slice + suggested config changes)? They also want quick mitigations to stop new 429s while we sort quota changes.

Priya K. (SRE): short-term mitigations: 1) ask customer to throttle client to their committed RPS, 2) temporarily increase token-bucket burst for their API key (we can do a one-off), or 3) enable emergency burst routing (route-level override) for next 30m. I'll prepare a one-off bucket bump if they approve.

Sasha L. (infra): I'll prepare the Grafana snapshot. Command I used to extract logs for the window: ```bash
jq -r 'select(.customer=="acme-inc-42")' /var/log/quotas-service/quotas-2026-02-18.log | sed -n '1,200p'
```

David R. (eng): also include trace from request-id they provided (x-request-id header). That will show end-to-end: gateway -> quota-enforcer -> router -> runtime. Example trace snippet: 
```
trace: id=9f3a route=/v1/generate/fast-chat-3 key=sa-acme-main events=[gateway:received -> quota:checked(0tokens) -> gateway:429 -> router:soft-shed]
```

Maya S.: perfect. I'll reply to acme with: explanation of layers, dashboard snapshot, log slice, trace, suggested config (increase burst or daily commit), and offer the temporary one-off bucket bump.

Priya K. (SRE): ETA for Grafana snapshot + log slice + proposed one-off config: 20–30m. I'll also draft the exact rationale lines you can paste.

infra-bot: scheduled job: grafana/snapshots/create acme-inc-42 1768901234 -> snapshot://GRAFANA/abc123 (expires 7d) :white_check_mark:

Sasha L. (infra): snapshot here: https://grafana.redwood.ai/snapshot/abc123, logs uploaded to secure-support-bucket/slices/acme-inc-42/1768901234.log.gz, and I attached the CSV of 429 events.

Maya S.: thanks everyone — I'll send to customer and close after they ack. If they want a permanent increase we'll follow our quota-change flow (billing & capacity validation).

David R. (eng): follow-up action items:
- Priya: prepare one-off burst bump plan and approval text.
- Sasha: confirm that dedicated pool mapping is correct for acme-inc-42 (so we know they actually had the reserved capacity applied).
- Maya: customer comms draft.

Maya S.: noted. I'll update thread when customer responds. Thanks!
